newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA'S JOBLESS EASE TO 14.2 PCT IN JUNE.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA'S JOBLESS EASE TO 14.2 PCT IN JUNE.

text.p: The number of the unemployed in
Bulgaria fell to 541,599 or 14.2 percent of the workforce in
June from 567,320 in May, a National Labour Exchange (NLE)
official said on Tuesday.
"Unemployment dipped last month because of the seasonal
jobs offered in the farming areas," the official told Reuters.
She said that seasonal employment will reduce the number of
jobless people until September.
Year-on-year unemployment figures showed a growing trend as
the new reformist government began implementing structural
reforms pledged to multylateral lenders.
Under preliminary NLE estimates some 160,000 employees in
the public sector and industrial enterprises are expected to be
laid off this year after the government closes down state loss
making firms and restructures production in others.
The World Bank has approved a $25 million loan for
severance payments and compensation for professional
retraining, and a further $80 million has been earmarked for
lending to private entrepreneurs.
Bulgaria's average unemployment rate for 1996 was 11.1
percent, down 0.3 points from 1995. Unemployment peaked in
January 1994, when 16.6 percent of the workforce was jobless.
